clue.text: Inclination to harpoon grand American whale

indicators.note: a harpoon pierces its target and lodges inside it, so one piece is driven into the middle of the other

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for grand, a thousand
US is short for the United States
a ramp is a slope or incline

explanation.surface: A whaler is keen to harpoon a big American whale.
explanation.walkthrough: The slope goes inside the outer letters, between G and US, giving GRAMPUS. 'Grand' looks like an adjective for the whale but is the abbreviation G.
explanation.definitionFit: A grampus is a kind of dolphin-like cetacean, Risso's dolphin or formerly the orca, so it counts as a whale.

clue.text: Good folk taking things steadily are risk takers

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
people who walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A paradox: careful, steady people turn out to be the ones taking chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking things steadily' sounds like caution, but it is literal: amblers walk slowly. G for good goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who bet money or chance outcomes are people who accept hazard, the plain meaning of the plural noun.

clue.text: A dispute with repeated opening point

parts.note: the opening letter of the word for dispute, R, given a second time in front of it
a row is a noisy quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: An argument keeps restarting at the same opening point.
explanation.walkthrough: The dispute is a row, and its opening letter is said twice, so a second R stands before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow is a pointer or sign showing direction, so it points the way, the noun sense of point.

clue.text: Very quiet religious mission sent out to cover America

indicators.note: to cover means the other letters go round America's abbreviation

parts.note: pi is informal British slang for pious or religious

indicators.note: sent out means dispatched in all directions, so the letters of mission are scattered

explanation.surface: A pious mission is quietly dispatched to the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: PI as slang for pious is a crossword favourite. The religious word and the scattered mission together 'cover' America, which sits just after PI.
explanation.definitionFit: Pianissimo is the musical direction, from Italian, telling a player to perform very softly.

clue.text: Relief only after securing account

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: sole means only or single
AC is the usual abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Someone feels relief only once their bank account is secured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like it fixes an order, but it only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is comfort in distress, the easing of grief or anxiety, which is what relief offers.

clue.text: Giving new face to seductress in capital of Germany

parts.note: a vamp is a woman who seduces men
taken as written

indicators.note: a capital letter is the one at the head of a word, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the country name

explanation.surface: A femme fatale gets a makeover in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Germany' tempts Berlin or Bonn, but here it is just the capital letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: To vamp is to renovate or patch up, originally fitting a new upper front to a shoe, so it means refurbishing.

clue.text: Long-standing conflict? Former soldier cheers, welcoming conclusion

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a vet is a veteran, in American usage
end and conclusion are synonyms
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: An old soldier raises a glass to the end of a long war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' suggests a toast, but here it is British informal thanks; vet for veteran is American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud, often between families, that may last generations.

clue.text: Jazz composer premieres in Manhattan — one nods knowingly

indicators.note: a premiere is a first showing, so the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A jazz composer's New York debut has an audience member nodding in recognition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premieres' suggests first performances in New York, but it picks the first letters of the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelonious Monk was an American pianist and composer, one of the founders of bebop.

clue.text: Shed light on botched raid — indignant about that

indicators.note: about means the word for indignant goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: irate means angry and indignant

indicators.note: a botched job is bungled, so the letters of raid are jumbled

explanation.surface: A failed police raid leaves someone angry and keen to expose what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link pointing back to the botched raid, which the angry word wraps round. 'Shed light on' sounds like exposing a scandal, but it is the literal sense of shining on.
explanation.definitionFit: To irradiate is to illuminate or shine light upon something, as well as to expose it to radiation.

clue.text: One provoking guard regularly having to flee

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters
to fly is to run away

explanation.surface: A sentry keeps being needled and has to run off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' sounds like how often the guard flees, but it picks alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a person who persistently annoys or stirs others into action, from the biting insect.

clue.text: Lunar features in large part of planet, I start to admit

indicators.note: large part of means most of the word, so the planet loses its last letter

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of admit

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to features on the moon lying across much of a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The planet is Mars, cut by 'large part of' to MAR; 'start to' takes A from admit. Moon and planet keep it astronomical, which makes the planet easy to miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria, plural of mare, are the dark basaltic plains on the moon once taken for seas.

clue.text: Former city tending to oust a radical

indicators.note: to oust means to push out, so the letter A is driven out of the word for tending

parts.note: leaning, as in leaning towards an opinion, means tending
rad is short for radical, in politics and in chemistry

explanation.surface: A city that once leaned to the left forces out a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to oust' drops the A from LEANING to leave LENING. Radical fits the Soviet picture, but it only gives RAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Leningrad was the Soviet name for St Petersburg from 1924 until 1991, so it is a city name no longer in use.

clue.text: Somehow depict howl in a deep voice

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the clue phrase is adverbial

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged in an unspecified order

parts.note: ten letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor tries to portray a howl using a bass voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of the two words rearrange; the hyphen comes from the enumeration.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-pitched sound has a low frequency, as a bass voice does, deep rather than shrill.

clue.text: Independent revitalised old star?

indicators.note: to revitalise is to remake something with new life, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for independent
three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper has revived a faded celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Independent hints at this newspaper, but it only gives I. The question mark marks the definition as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a much-admired celebrity, a famous figure fans worship, just like a star.

clue.text: Guitar? Aim to play it idly for a time

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: intent is aim or purpose
T is the abbreviation for time
to brush casually across the strings of a guitar

explanation.surface: Advice to a guitarist to aim at playing lazily for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: In INTENT, the first T is swapped for STRUM. 'For a time' looks like 'for a while', but it says 'in place of a T'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guitar is one example of a musical instrument, so the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Most of orders provided by right-wing forces will be in error

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter

parts.note: a remit is the orders or instructions a person is given
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary force, the extreme right wing in arms

explanation.surface: Orders handed down by far-right forces turn out to be mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts REMIT to REMI. SS, the Nazi Schutzstaffel, is a crossword stand-by for right-wing forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless of duty, so someone remiss is at fault in error.

clue.text: Source of flour? Woman accepting dicky quality

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman
dicky is British slang for weak or unwell, as in a dicky heart
tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: Where does flour come from? A woman with a dodgy quality, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British informal for weak or unsound, as in a dicky heart; it is not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstone is the heavy stone that grinds grain into meal in a mill, hence where meal comes from.

clue.text: Nationalists backing South Africa's verse

indicators.note: going backwards means the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: Nats is informal for nationalists
ZA is the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: Nationalist politicians support a poem written in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like political support but turns the word around. ZA comes from Zuid-Afrika.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines in a poem; verse can mean such a unit of poetry.

clue.text: Hesitation shown by bird, unknown, seen around south of France

indicators.note: seen around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
the Midi is the south of France
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A bird hesitates while a stranger watches it in southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' is not the letter S: the Midi is the French name for the southern region.
explanation.definitionFit: Timidity is shyness or lack of courage, which shows as a reluctance or holding back.

clue.text: One's press release will include line of questionable delicacy

parts.note: one is, I am, contracted to I'm

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: PR is press relations or publicity
a rope is a line, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A press release contains a line in poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Line in the sense of cord, not a line of text; 'One's' contracts 'one is' to 'I am'.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper describes behaviour or remarks that breach decency or good taste, lacking propriety.

clue.text: Clear evidence of injury I had

parts.note: a limp shows a leg injury
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone admits there was clear proof of a hurt they suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear' looks like an adjective for the evidence, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid means transparent or unclouded, as in water or prose that is easy to see through.

clue.text: A lot of pages applied to the way to watch movies now?

indicators.note: applied to means put onto something else, so one piece comes after the other

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Is reading lots of pages the way to watch films today?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way to' reads as one phrase, but 'the way' is ST and 'to' only joins it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stream is to play video over the internet as it downloads, the current method for viewing films.

clue.text: Orchestral piece, informally — a rich source, containing heart of Elgar, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run in the opposite order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a mine is a rich source, as in a mine of information

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letter is taken

parts.note: the central letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: On reflection, Elgar's famous orchestral work holds a rich vein of his genius.
explanation.walkthrough: MINE takes G after its M, A goes in front, and AMGINE reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's Enigma Variations is commonly shortened to Enigma, the informal name of that orchestral work.

clue.text: Writer seen around street cafe

indicators.note: seen around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An author is spotted in a street cafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' wants to be a person, but here it is a pen: a Biro, the British word for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant or café serving simple food and drink.

clue.text: Ability to track meaningless bits of data I ignored

indicators.note: ignored means left out of account, so the letter I is dropped

parts.note: noise is the unwanted random signal that carries no information in a set of data

explanation.surface: Tracking ability depends on filtering out meaningless data and one's own ego.
explanation.walkthrough: In data science noise is random variation with no meaning; 'ignored' drops the I from it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose is a keen sense of smell or instinct for tracking things down, as in a nose for news.

clue.text: One vehicle's crashed through screen? Keep talking

indicators.note: to crash through something is to end up inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to screen is to filter, or a filter is a screen
a bus is a vehicle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A vehicle crashes through a screen and someone goes on talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has', a link; 'screen' is the verb sense of sifting, as a filter does.
explanation.definitionFit: To filibuster is to make prolonged speeches in a legislature to delay or block a vote.

clue.text: Part of glove so cut down by doctor

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: thus means so, in that way
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A glove is trimmed down by a doctor in surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' shortens THUS to THU, and the doctor is MB, the Bachelor of Medicine degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A glove has a separate sheath for the thumb, the short thick digit set apart from the fingers.

clue.text: Quickly eat sandwich with zero content?

indicators.note: content is what is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Wolfing a sandwich with nothing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: BLT holds O: B(O)LT. The question mark is because 'zero content' sounds like an empty sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to gulp it down hurriedly, swallowing without chewing properly.

clue.text: It's Google that's replaced scientist

indicators.note: things replaced are put back in a different position, so the letters change places

parts.note: nine letters rearranged, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A search engine has supplanted the expert.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'It's' is ignored, giving nine letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A geologist studies rocks and the structure of the Earth, one branch of natural science.

clue.text: Witty comment getting behind English kit

indicators.note: to get behind something is to come after it, so the order is fixed

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: A wisecrack supporting the England kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kit' looks like a noun, the England strip, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To kit out means to supply with gear or clothing, the same as to furnish someone.

clue.text: European right to interrupt associate sharply

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an ally is an associate
E is the abbreviation for European
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A European conservative sharply interrupts a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: E and RT go inside ALLY: AL(ERT)LY. 'Right' is just the abbreviation, not a political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something alertly means with keen, quick attention, the watchful sense of sharply.

clue.text: Military leader not yet promoted? Leader of regiment for 31 days

parts.note: OC is officer commanding
an OC who has not yet got the job is an OC-to-be

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: A junior officer awaits promotion and temporarily leads a regiment for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone not yet promoted to OC is an OC-to-be, giving OC + TO BE; the question mark flags this playful step.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the year has thirty-one days, so the period identifies it among the long months.
